A 15 ppm bilge alarm and stopping device.en: A 15 ppm bilge alarm and stopping device are part of an approved oily-water separation arrangement, but equipment approval never overrides MARPOL discharge conditions or local restrictions.

A 4–20 mA live-zero loop represents zero.en: A 4–20 mA live-zero loop represents zero span at 4 mA and full span at 20 mA. Current below normal range may indicate a fault; transmitter scaling and loop wiring must be verified.

A bill of lading may evidence receipt, c.en: A bill of lading may evidence receipt, contract terms and title-related rights. The person signing must be authorised and must not knowingly certify an inaccurate cargo description or condition.

A Bourdon gauge measures pressure throug.en: A Bourdon gauge measures pressure through elastic tube deformation; piezoelectric sensors are generally suited to dynamic pressure measurement and typically require conditioning. A displayed 0 bar may reflect failed instrumentation rather than zero line pressure.

A cold-front passage can involve rapid w.en: A cold-front passage can involve rapid wind veer/backing, pressure changes and convective weather; warm fronts often bring more layered cloud and extensive precipitation. Actual weather depends on the system and locality.

A dedicated lookout supports detection b.en: A dedicated lookout supports detection by sight and hearing under Rule 5 and must report changes clearly; helm, chart and radar duties can impede an effective lookout when workload rises.

A draft survey derives displacement chan.en: A draft survey derives displacement changes from corrected drafts and hydrostatics, then adjusts for non-cargo weights such as ballast, freshwater, fuel and stores. Water density changes the interpretation of tabulated displacement.

A drill is meaningful when crew actions,.en: A drill is meaningful when crew actions, timing, communication, access and equipment limitations are observed. Completion of a checklist is not evidence that the response would work under real failure conditions.

A final departure stability check must u.en: A final departure stability check must use actual cargo, fuel, water, ballast, free-surface states and shipboard draughts. A previously approved loadcase can become invalid after any substantial late shift of a high or longitudinally displaced weight.

A fixed CO₂ installation suppresses fire.en: A fixed CO₂ installation suppresses fire by displacing oxygen and can be lethal to anyone in the protected space. Release decisions require proper command, evacuation checks and strict access control.

A lifeboat is a survival craft, while a.en: A lifeboat is a survival craft, while a rescue boat is intended for recovering persons and marshalling survival craft; some installations may meet both roles. Launching procedures are equipment-specific and require trained crew.

A longitudinal moment moves the vessel a.en: A longitudinal moment moves the vessel away from its initial trim and can be estimated using MCT 1 cm when the loading instrument's assumptions are respected. Signs and draft distribution require LCF and vessel-specific data.

A meridian altitude of the Sun can suppo.en: A meridian altitude of the Sun can support latitude estimation using corrected noon altitude and the Sun's declination, with hemisphere and zenith-side interpretation required. This is a simplified navigation-school geometry case.

A rhumb line crosses all meridians at a.en: A rhumb line crosses all meridians at a constant true bearing, appearing straight on a Mercator chart. It does not generally provide the shortest spherical route, especially on long ocean passages at higher latitude.

A running fix transfers an earlier posit.en: A running fix transfers an earlier position line to the time of a second observation using estimated course, speed and set/drift. Both fixes and transfer errors affect reliability.

A tensioned mooring line stores energy t.en: A tensioned mooring line stores energy throughout its length; a failed rope, fitting or line of pull can sweep a large area. Painted snap-back zones cannot represent every real failure path.

A tidal window is the period when actual.en: A tidal window is the period when actual depth and operational restrictions permit passage. It depends on chart datum, forecast tide, squat, uncertainty and required UKC, which may change with speed and sea state.

A tug's useful force depends on thrust d.en: A tug's useful force depends on thrust direction, towline geometry and safe connection arrangements; rated bollard pull is not automatically available as lateral force at the ship's hull.

A VHF DSC distress alert on Channel 70 i.en: A VHF DSC distress alert on Channel 70 is a digital alert, not the subsequent spoken distress message. Radiotelephony distress traffic normally uses Channel 16 unless the situation and instructions dictate otherwise.

AC generators must meet prescribed volta.en: AC generators must meet prescribed voltage, frequency, phase sequence and phase-angle conditions for parallel connection. A closing error can produce damaging transients, torque and reverse-power events.

AC synchronising requires compatible vol.en: AC synchronising requires compatible voltage, frequency, phase sequence and phase angle before a generator breaker closes on a live bus. Out-of-phase closing may cause damaging torque and currents.

Advection fog forms when warm moist air.en: Advection fog forms when warm moist air moves over a colder surface, cooling below its dew point. Radiation fog typically arises through nocturnal cooling; sea visibility reductions need not coincide with precipitation.

AIS supplies transmitted identity and mo.en: AIS supplies transmitted identity and movement data but is not an independent collision avoidance sensor. GNSS input failures, erroneous static data and human edits can mislead the bridge.

Alarm Monitoring Systems observe sensor.en: Alarm Monitoring Systems observe sensor and control signals, but alarm acknowledgement is not fault rectification. A single high-level alarm may arise from real flooding, bad sensors, wiring or data transport.

An echo sounder measures acoustic travel.en: An echo sounder measures acoustic travel time to a reflecting surface; depth readout may be below the transducer or adjusted to a different reference. Draft, squat, offset, sound speed and seabed shape affect clearance.

An insulated-neutral ship distribution s.en: An insulated-neutral ship distribution system may remain in operation after a first earth fault while giving an insulation warning. A second fault on another phase can create dangerous fault current; the actual arrangement and protection must be identified from drawings.

An open-loop control output does not aut.en: An open-loop control output does not automatically correct for deviation, while closed-loop feedback compares a measured variable with a setpoint and adjusts the actuator. Sensor fault can defeat feedback despite normal controller operation.

Anchor watch combines movement monitorin.en: Anchor watch combines movement monitoring with depth, tide, weather, chain direction and nearby traffic. GNSS position alarms must account for vessel swing and the location of the antenna relative to the anchor.

Anchor watch uses planned swinging circl.en: Anchor watch uses planned swinging circle, actual chain length, fixing uncertainty and observed trends. Radius is not simply the number of shackles paid out: chain catenary, depth, hull length and weather affect the envelope.

Anchoring must consider holding ground,.en: Anchoring must consider holding ground, water depth, current, weather, planned swinging room and actual cable condition. The planned paid-out chain length is not the same as the vessel's distance from the anchor.

Annex III addresses harmful substances i.en: Annex III addresses harmful substances in packaged form, with marine pollutant identification and packaging, marking, documentation and stowage provisions implemented through the IMDG Code.

Apparent wind is the true wind vector re.en: Apparent wind is the true wind vector relative to the ship's movement through the relevant reference frame. Direction and reference source matter: ship heading, ground track and sensor corrections must not be confused.

Appraisal precedes detailed route design.en: Appraisal precedes detailed route design: chart coverage and quality, weather, tidal stream, services, machinery constraints and reporting requirements determine whether a proposed passage is feasible.

Azimuth is the true bearing of a celesti.en: Azimuth is the true bearing of a celestial or terrestrial object clockwise from true north, with corrections for observer position, time and ephemeris when celestial. It can help determine gyro or compass error when observation geometry is valid.

Ballast treatment and exchange are diffe.en: Ballast treatment and exchange are different compliance approaches. Operational decisions depend on the ship's approved Ballast Water Management Plan, treatment limitations, log entries and local port requirements.

Battery charging profiles depend on chem.en: Battery charging profiles depend on chemistry, ambient temperature, ventilation and control limits. Afloat and absorption charging must use compatible equipment; overcharge can generate heat/gas or shorten service life.

Battery thermal runaway can spread betwe.en: Battery thermal runaway can spread between cells while producing heat, flammable gases and toxic decomposition products. Chemistry-specific maker instructions and installed detection/suppression systems govern response.

Bay-row-tier slot codes locate container.en: Bay-row-tier slot codes locate containers in the stowage plan; load distribution, GM, stack-weight limits, lashing loads and verified gross mass are separate checks.

Beaufort is an observational wind-force.en: Beaufort is an observational wind-force scale; actual measured wind speed depends on averaging interval, instrument exposure and gust characteristics. Sea state is only a supporting observation, especially with swell or restricted fetch.

Biofouling and antifouling controls affe.en: Biofouling and antifouling controls affect invasive species and coatings, while ship recycling has separate hazardous-material and facility requirements. The IMO Hong Kong Convention entered into force on 26 June 2025; implementation depends on scope and administration.

Bridge Resource Management uses challeng.en: Bridge Resource Management uses challenge-response, explicit task allocation and shared situational awareness; alarms are prompts to investigate, not replacements for human cross-checks.

Buoyancy equals the weight of displaced.en: Buoyancy equals the weight of displaced water in equilibrium; displacement volume must be multiplied by the actual water density. Different seawater and dockwater densities give different immersed volumes for the same floating mass.

Cargo plans must satisfy local structura.en: Cargo plans must satisfy local structural loading, longitudinal strength, trim and intact stability as well as deck-space geometry. Two cargo plans with the same total mass can impose very different bending and shear forces.

Cargo restraint is designed for accelera.en: Cargo restraint is designed for accelerations produced by ship motions. A simple mass-times-acceleration estimate illustrates load, but selecting lashings also requires angles, friction, securing-point capacity and the ship's approved Cargo Securing Manual.

Cargo sweat and ship sweat arise from di.en: Cargo sweat and ship sweat arise from differing temperature and moisture conditions. The decision to ventilate depends on cargo properties, external air dew point and measured hold conditions, not simply on outside relative humidity.

Cascade control uses an outer controller.en: Cascade control uses an outer controller setting an inner-loop target; feedforward acts on a measured disturbance. The inner loop must remain reliable or the outer system may amplify an uncorrected process fault.

Chart course should be measured against.en: Chart course should be measured against the meridian/compass rose using the correct true reference; magnetically steered headings require separately applied variation and deviation. Bearing orientation from a chart is not automatically a corrected compass order.

Chart Datum is the reference surface fro.en: Chart Datum is the reference surface from which charted depths are normally measured. Tide heights above the applicable chart datum may be combined with chart depths for a static depth estimate, but LAT is not a synonym for every national chart datum.

CII is an operational carbon-intensity i.en: CII is an operational carbon-intensity indicator based on emissions and transport-work-related activity under a specified methodology. Lower total fuel consumption in isolation does not guarantee a better intensity indicator.

Closed-loop communication requires a pre.en: Closed-loop communication requires a precise instruction, correct read-back and explicit confirmation. The loop is especially important when similar machinery numbers or valve designations can be confused.

Closer isobar spacing in a fixed map sca.en: Closer isobar spacing in a fixed map scale often implies a stronger horizontal pressure gradient and stronger geostrophic wind, subject to latitude, surface friction and synoptic structure.

COLREG navigation lights have defined se.en: COLREG navigation lights have defined sectors, colours and minimum ranges based on vessel class and size. Geographical detection distance also depends on meteorological visibility and height of eye; a light's legal nominal range is not the distance at which every observer will see it.

COLREG Rule 13 obliges the overtaking ve.en: COLREG Rule 13 obliges the overtaking vessel to keep out of the way until finally past and clear. An approaching vessel more than 22.5° abaft another's beam is overtaking; doubt must be resolved conservatively.

COLREG Rule 15 identifies a crossing enc.en: COLREG Rule 15 identifies a crossing encounter between two power-driven vessels in sight. Risk assessment still depends on bearing trend, range, visual observation and all available sensors, not a single ARPA number.

COLREG Rule 6 requires safe speed approp.en: COLREG Rule 6 requires safe speed appropriate to conditions, including visibility, density of traffic, manoeuvrability, background light, weather and proximity of navigational hazards. There is no universally lawful fixed speed for restricted visibility.

COLREG Rules 5–8 apply across the routin.en: COLREG Rules 5–8 apply across the routine collision-avoidance decision chain: effective lookout, safe speed, risk assessment with all available means, and timely substantial action. Later encounter rules do not replace those fundamentals.

Control-loop tuning balances response ti.en: Control-loop tuning balances response time, stability, noise and actuator wear. A process that oscillates after maintenance may have altered sensor scaling or actuator dynamics, not merely inappropriate PID coefficients.

Corrective maintenance after breakdown p.en: Corrective maintenance after breakdown prioritises safe isolation, effect on essential services and systematic root-cause assessment. Restoring a machine to operation without checking the cause risks repeated or more severe failure.

Corrosion morphology can indicate differ.en: Corrosion morphology can indicate different mechanisms: galvanic corrosion depends on coupled dissimilar metals and electrolyte, while crevice corrosion may concentrate inside poorly ventilated gaps. Surface coating alone is not diagnosis.

Cospas-Sarsat 406 MHz alerts are process.en: Cospas-Sarsat 406 MHz alerts are processed through the satellite segment and ground network, then forwarded through LUT/MCC arrangements to responsible SAR coordination authorities. The beacon's GNSS position and independent satellite-derived location are not identical data sources.

Crane Safe Working Load and rigging capa.en: Crane Safe Working Load and rigging capacities apply under stated configurations and load paths. Sling angles increase tension as the angle to horizontal decreases, while dynamic effects and actual equipment limits remain critical.

Critical-equipment identification consid.en: Critical-equipment identification considers consequence of failure, available redundancy, detection and restoration time, not simply purchase price or physical size.

Cross-track error (XTE) is the lateral d.en: Cross-track error (XTE) is the lateral displacement from the active intended route leg, not a replacement for position uncertainty or danger-clearance limits. Turns, antenna offsets and chart accuracy also affect the interpretation.

Cumulonimbus clouds have strong vertical.en: Cumulonimbus clouds have strong vertical growth and may bring squalls, intense precipitation, lightning, gust fronts and sudden visibility change. The cloud's visible shape is evidence of convective activity but does not determine precise wind speed.

Cylinder-head maintenance requires engin.en: Cylinder-head maintenance requires engine cooling, pressure release, residual-fuel assessment, lifting plan and correct bolt preload sequence. A visual absence of leaks does not demonstrate safe lifting or correct reassembly.

Damage control requires monitored ingres.en: Damage control requires monitored ingress rates, boundary integrity and stability throughout the response. Pump operation, intentional transfers and counterflooding can affect free-surface and longitudinal stability in unexpected ways.

Dangerous goods transport combines accur.en: Dangerous goods transport combines accurate classification and declaration with package condition, documentation, stowage, segregation and emergency response. An identical UN number does not remove the need to check packing group and special provisions.

DC motor speed and torque characteristic.en: DC motor speed and torque characteristics depend on excitation and drive design. A series-excited DC motor can overspeed dangerously with loss of load; separately excited units depend on field integrity.

Departure is the east–west distance alon.en: Departure is the east–west distance along a local parallel, measured in NM, and is related to DLo via the cosine of latitude. It differs from east–west change in geodetic longitude, which is angular.

Direct-on-line induction motor starting.en: Direct-on-line induction motor starting draws significant inrush and starting torque, while star-delta starters and VFDs change the starting electrical and mechanical behaviour. Equipment compatibility and starting load torque matter.

Distress (MAYDAY), urgency (PAN PAN) and.en: Distress (MAYDAY), urgency (PAN PAN) and safety (SECURITE) communications represent different priorities and procedures. DSC alerting and follow-up radiotelephony use the relevant equipment and working channels; actual distress calls must never be used for drills.

DR advances a previous position by headi.en: DR advances a previous position by heading and speed through water; EP can additionally include estimated effects of current, wind and leeway. Their uncertainty grows with elapsed time without an independent fix.

Drydock preparation coordinates class su.en: Drydock preparation coordinates class survey items, hull inspections, sea valves, cathodic protection, anchors and shaft arrangements. Isolation planning must be established before exposure of sea-connected equipment.

Earth-leakage protective arrangements de.en: Earth-leakage protective arrangements detect residual current or insulation failure according to the installed earthing system. Correct device selection and testing depend on supply arrangement, load and protection zones.

ECDIS safety settings depend on the actu.en: ECDIS safety settings depend on the actual maximum draught, available chart depth and tide, squat, survey quality and company UKC policy. Safety contour and safety depth serve different presentation and alert functions.

ECDIS, radar and AIS are complementary b.en: ECDIS, radar and AIS are complementary but can share common heading, log and position errors. Independent cross-checks are based on distinct principles, not just different display brands.

Emergency logs should preserve observed.en: Emergency logs should preserve observed facts, communications and ordered actions with timestamps. Estimates and assumptions must be identified; accurate records support coordination and later investigation without delaying life-saving work.

Enclosed spaces can contain oxygen-defic.en: Enclosed spaces can contain oxygen-deficient, toxic or flammable atmospheres despite looking clean. An entry permit and gas test are control measures, not guarantees that the atmosphere will stay safe.

Enclosed-space casualty response require.en: Enclosed-space casualty response requires stopping a second uncontrolled entry, making a rescue plan and ensuring suitable atmosphere assessment and breathing protection. IMO revised enclosed-space recommendations stress additional permits for energy isolation and task-specific hazards.

Engine-room handover is a transfer of op.en: Engine-room handover is a transfer of operational risk awareness, not merely a signature. It should communicate plant status, isolations, alarms, planned work, temporary arrangements and escalation triggers.

ETA is driven by distance over ground di.en: ETA is driven by distance over ground divided by SOG, and through-water speed plus current may vary along the route. Fuel use depends on machinery loading and operating hours, so less time does not always imply proportional fuel savings.

Explosion-protected equipment suitabilit.en: Explosion-protected equipment suitability depends on the hazardous-area classification, gas/dust group, temperature class and protection concept. Damaged glands, incorrect spares and unapproved maintenance can invalidate protection.

Failure management must distinguish disp.en: Failure management must distinguish display, transducer, data bus and electrical supply faults. Backup navigation is only credible if equipment independence and competent procedures have been verified.

Fire integrity depends on A/B class divi.en: Fire integrity depends on A/B class divisions, penetrations, dampers, fire doors and detection zones as actually approved for the vessel. Fire ratings are not the same as a guarantee of unlimited fire resistance.

Fire-tube boilers route hot combustion p.en: Fire-tube boilers route hot combustion products through tubes surrounded by water, while water-tube designs circulate water/steam inside tubes exposed to hot gases. Both require correctly set water-level safeguards and blowdown plans.

Flash point is the lowest temperature at.en: Flash point is the lowest temperature at which a liquid produces sufficient vapour to ignite under a specified standard test; it is not the autoignition temperature and does not independently describe all storage hazards.

Flooding response combines watertight in.en: Flooding response combines watertight integrity, source identification, stability awareness, tank soundings and boundary integrity. Pump capacity can be exceeded by rising ingress even if a bilge alarm is acknowledged.

For a conventional synchronous alternato.en: For a conventional synchronous alternator, system frequency tracks shaft rotational speed and pole count; the governor regulates speed/real-power sharing while the AVR predominantly controls voltage/reactive-power behaviour.

GMDSS-approved mobile satellite terminal.en: GMDSS-approved mobile satellite terminals carry defined distress and safety functions within their recognised coverage. A vessel's commercial satellite internet access is not automatically a certified GMDSS alerting route.

GNSS geometric dilution of precision is.en: GNSS geometric dilution of precision is only one contributor to position uncertainty; orbit, timing, atmosphere, multipath, spoofing and equipment integrity also matter. Multiple displays sharing one sensor are not independent checks.

GNSS reliability can be affected by spoo.en: GNSS reliability can be affected by spoofing, jamming, multipath, antenna failure and shared sensor feeds. Multiple screens agreeing is not independent corroboration if they use the same receiver or antenna.

Grain cargo can shift in partly filled s.en: Grain cargo can shift in partly filled spaces and create heeling moments, so grain-stability requirements and approved loading conditions differ from ordinary solid bulk treatment.

Grounding creates local loads and potent.en: Grounding creates local loads and potential hull damage; refloating plans depend on verified bathymetry, tidal state, hull condition, stability and environmental consequences. Immediate full-astern power can worsen damage.

Gyrocompass and magnetic compass provide.en: Gyrocompass and magnetic compass provide distinct heading references. Gyro error changes with instrument state, speed/latitude influences, installation and sensor failures; it should not be treated as zero because it is electronic.

GZ is the horizontal lever between weigh.en: GZ is the horizontal lever between weight and buoyancy lines of action at a given angle of heel. Righting moment equals displacement weight multiplied by GZ under the corresponding units and assumptions.

HDOP describes how satellite geometry am.en: HDOP describes how satellite geometry amplifies horizontal ranging uncertainty. It is dimensionless and is not itself a position error in metres; receiver quality, interference, corrections and multipath also matter.

High-voltage marine electrical systems r.en: High-voltage marine electrical systems require authorised switching, isolation, testing for dead and earthing where specified. The correct safe state is established by the vessel's approved procedures and equipment ratings.

High-voltage shore connection must coord.en: High-voltage shore connection must coordinate voltage, frequency, phase sequence, grounding and protections between ship and terminal under an approved transfer plan. Galvanic and fault-current hazards are separate considerations.

Ho is observed celestial altitude after.en: Ho is observed celestial altitude after appropriate index, dip and astronomical corrections; Hc is computed altitude for an assumed position and ephemeris. The difference is an intercept in arcminutes and approximately nautical miles.

Hydrostatic gauge pressure increases wit.en: Hydrostatic gauge pressure increases with liquid density and vertical depth below a free surface. In a ventilated tank, p = ρgh applies to the column, not to vessel roll, acceleration or an air-pressurised space.

IMSBC Group A includes cargoes liable to.en: IMSBC Group A includes cargoes liable to liquefy or dynamically separate under relevant moisture conditions. Shipper documents and sampling arrangements matter; the master should not rely on the cargo looking dry.

In a head-on encounter between two power.en: In a head-on encounter between two power-driven vessels in sight and involving collision risk, Rule 14 requires each to alter course to starboard so that they pass port-to-port. Rules 5–8 still govern lookout, assessment and effective action.

In an ideal rectangular slack tank, tran.en: In an ideal rectangular slack tank, transverse free-surface moment scales with length times breadth cubed; actual tank shape, fill, baffles and liquid density modify the approved tabulated moment. Volume alone is insufficient.

In restricted visibility the officer mus.en: In restricted visibility the officer must assess risk with a proper lookout, safe speed and radar as applicable; COLREG Rule 19 is not a simple right-of-way chart copied from vessels in sight.

In restricted visibility, COLREG Rule 19.en: In restricted visibility, COLREG Rule 19 requires safe speed and risk assessment using all available means; fog signals are separate from radar target detection and must follow the vessel's actual navigational condition.

In the Northern Hemisphere the right sem.en: In the Northern Hemisphere the right semicircle relative to tropical cyclone motion is often the more dangerous due to rotational wind and storm translation. Forecast-track uncertainty, sea room and vessel speed make simple manoeuvre mnemonics insufficient.

In tropical cyclones, the eye may be com.en: In tropical cyclones, the eye may be comparatively calmer while the eyewall contains intense winds and heavy rain. A temporary lull does not imply that the storm has passed.

Initial metacentric height GM = KM minus.en: Initial metacentric height GM = KM minus KG at the loading draught. Free-surface correction lowers effective GM; small-angle positive GM alone cannot certify the entire righting-arm or damage-stability behaviour.

Insulation monitoring detects deteriorat.en: Insulation monitoring detects deterioration on certain marine insulated distribution systems. An alarm may occur without immediate breaker operation, so controlled investigation and electronic equipment protection are essential.

KG changes as a moment-weighted average.en: KG changes as a moment-weighted average when weights are added, shifted or removed. The final displacement changes with added mass, but not with movement of existing mass. Free-surface correction is considered separately.

Knot suitability depends on intended loa.en: Knot suitability depends on intended load, rope construction, bend radius, slip resistance and approved use. A correctly tied demonstration knot is not necessarily a certified cargo-lifting termination.

Latitude change and longitude change are.en: Latitude change and longitude change are signed angular differences. For local-plane navigation, departure ≈ DLo(minutes) × cos(mean latitude), and distance is the vector magnitude of DLat and departure.

Latitude is angular distance north or so.en: Latitude is angular distance north or south of the equator. In conventional nautical chart work, one minute of latitude approximately equals one nautical mile in the north–south direction, subject to Earth-ellipsoid refinements.

Laytime calculations depend on the speci.en: Laytime calculations depend on the specific charter party: notice of readiness, commencement clauses, exceptions, reversible time and agreed treatment of weather or port delays. Demurrage/despatch is contractual, not a universal hourly rule.

Leeway is the sideways drift relative to.en: Leeway is the sideways drift relative to the water caused by wind and hull form; its direction and magnitude vary with vessel, speed, exposure and loading. It is distinct from water-current set/drift.

Linear interpolation estimates an interm.en: Linear interpolation estimates an intermediate value from two adjacent tabulated entries only when the parameter is smooth over the interval. It is not valid across discontinuities, turnpoints or regulatory threshold changes.

Liquefied-gas cargo operations involve t.en: Liquefied-gas cargo operations involve temperature, pressure, cargo compatibility and hazardous-area controls. Cargo transfer procedures depend on tank type and the vessel's approved cargo system and terminal interface.

Liquid free surfaces shift the effective.en: Liquid free surfaces shift the effective centre of gravity during heel; their stability-booklet free-surface moment produces a virtual rise in G. The correction depends on tank geometry, filling state and the approved calculation basis.

LNG propulsion introduces cryogenic, fir.en: LNG propulsion introduces cryogenic, fire, vapour-management and fuel-gas system hazards that depend on certified design and the applicable IGF/IGC requirements. Gaseous leaks can create hazardous atmospheres even if visible liquid is absent.

Locally generated wind sea typically tra.en: Locally generated wind sea typically tracks the local wind field, whereas swell may travel long distances from a remote storm. Multiple wave trains can produce uncomfortable rolling despite moderate measured wind.

Longitude is the angle east or west of t.en: Longitude is the angle east or west of the prime meridian; distance along a parallel shrinks as latitude increases. Crossing 180° requires the shorter signed difference, not naive arithmetic on E and W labels.

Longitudinal weight movement creates a t.en: Longitudinal weight movement creates a trimming moment and changes trim, with the response governed by hydrostatic MCT 1 cm and LCF. A simple estimate does not provide the individual forward and aft draught changes.

Lost containers can create a navigation.en: Lost containers can create a navigation hazard and may also pose pollution or dangerous-goods risks. Immediate response must follow the ship's emergency and reporting procedures while preserving safe navigation and evidence.

Low-speed two-stroke marine diesel engin.en: Low-speed two-stroke marine diesel engines rely on efficient scavenge-air supply while exhaust gas is being displaced. One power stroke per revolution does not guarantee adequate fresh air at every load.

Machinery-space bilge water discharge re.en: Machinery-space bilge water discharge requires compliance with the vessel's approved oil-filtering equipment arrangements, 15-ppm monitoring where applicable and additional operational, area and port restrictions. A ppm readout alone is not authorisation.

Magnetic variation is the angular differ.en: Magnetic variation is the angular difference between true and magnetic north, varying by area and time; compass deviation is the error associated with the individual ship's compass heading.

Maintenance planning must consider hours.en: Maintenance planning must consider hours, calendar dates, maker requirements and operating duty; a late task may require additional risk controls and company authorisation. Deferral is not the same as completion.

Marine gas oil (MGO) is a distillate fue.en: Marine gas oil (MGO) is a distillate fuel class; marine diesel oil (MDO) terminology may refer to different distillate blends and grades. Density, viscosity, sulphur, ignition and compatibility are determined by the delivered fuel analysis and OEM limits, not the commercial label alone.

Marine LNG, methanol and other alternati.en: Marine LNG, methanol and other alternative fuels have different flammability, toxicity, cryogenic and atmosphere-management hazards. Equipment-specific procedures, IGF/IGC requirements where applicable and crew training govern transfers.

Marine radar estimates target range from.en: Marine radar estimates target range from the round-trip time of radio pulses. X- and S-band radars have different propagation/rain and resolution characteristics; echo strength also depends on target geometry, shadowing and sea clutter.

Maritime cyber risk can affect GNSS, ECD.en: Maritime cyber risk can affect GNSS, ECDIS updates, PMS and cargo systems; operational safety requires segregation, trusted change management and a fallback when electronic inputs are questionable.

Maritime Safety Information is selected.en: Maritime Safety Information is selected by coverage area, transmission schedules and message category. NAVTEX at 518 kHz normally carries English MSI; regional or national-language services may use different frequencies.

MARPOL Annex II covers noxious liquid su.en: MARPOL Annex II covers noxious liquid substances carried in bulk, with cargo categorisation and discharge requirements based on the IBC Code, a ship's Procedures and Arrangements Manual and approved records.

MARPOL Annex IV sewage requirements vary.en: MARPOL Annex IV sewage requirements vary by plant approval, comminution/disinfection status, distance from nearest land and special provisions. Retention is the safe option when discharge conditions are uncertain.

MARPOL Annex V imposes different disposa.en: MARPOL Annex V imposes different disposal requirements by garbage category, area and distance from land. Plastics are prohibited from discharge into the sea; garbage segregation and record keeping remain operational controls.

MARPOL Annex VI controls ship air pollut.en: MARPOL Annex VI controls ship air pollutants and energy-efficiency compliance. Sulphur limits are typically 0.50% m/m outside relevant SOx ECAs and 0.10% m/m inside; the Mediterranean became a SOx ECA on 1 May 2025.

MARPOL has six technical Annexes, regula.en: MARPOL has six technical Annexes, regulating oil, noxious liquid bulk cargo, packaged marine pollutants, sewage, garbage and air emissions. Applicable vessel certificates and discharge records differ by Annex and ship type.

Mean latitude sailing approximates short.en: Mean latitude sailing approximates short or moderate passages using a mid-latitude cosine to convert longitude difference into departure. Its accuracy deteriorates with large changes in latitude, high-latitude geometry and long routes.

Meteorological and tidal currents may ch.en: Meteorological and tidal currents may change in both magnitude and direction. Set is the direction toward which current flows and drift is speed; the ship's COG/SOG differs from heading/log through water accordingly.

Methanol and ammonia require different t.en: Methanol and ammonia require different toxicity, flammability and materials/ventilation precautions; ship-specific approval, crew training and fuel-transfer instructions are critical. A generic 'alternative fuel' PPE set is insufficient.

MF/HF communications depend on propagati.en: MF/HF communications depend on propagation, chosen frequencies, antenna tuning, equipment status and the DSC watch arrangement. A nominal station range is not a reliable operational coverage guarantee.

Min-max inventory must cover lead time,.en: Min-max inventory must cover lead time, consumption, failure criticality and redundancy. A stock ledger can overstate usable spares when parts are expired, damaged or reserved for essential equipment.

Mooring hazards include stored elastic e.en: Mooring hazards include stored elastic energy, poor lead angles, mixed-line elasticity and damaged fittings. Snap-back paths vary with the actual line and hardware arrangement, not solely marked deck zones.

Motor protection must cover overload, st.en: Motor protection must cover overload, stalled rotor, phase loss, overheating and appropriate insulation condition. A protective trip records a symptom but needs diagnostic confirmation before restart.

Navigational warnings and permanent char.en: Navigational warnings and permanent chart corrections address different timescales. An ECDIS update status or a paper chart edition does not necessarily incorporate temporary hazards communicated by MSI.

Nonlinear drives draw nonsinusoidal curr.en: Nonlinear drives draw nonsinusoidal currents that generate harmonic distortion and heating; total harmonic distortion (THD) describes their relative content, but absolute current and network impedance determine actual stress.

Oil analysis combines viscosity, wear pa.en: Oil analysis combines viscosity, wear particles, water content and contamination trends. One out-of-range sample may indicate a developing fault or a sampling error; trend and source verification matter.

On a Mercator navigation chart, distance.en: On a Mercator navigation chart, distance should be taken from the latitude scale near the route, where one minute of latitude is approximately one nautical mile; paper chart distortion varies with latitude.

Operational technology runs critical pro.en: Operational technology runs critical propulsion, power and cargo systems and requires controlled changes, validated firmware and secure vendor access. A legitimate-looking USB drive may introduce unsafe software.

Orifice differential-pressure meters inf.en: Orifice differential-pressure meters infer flow from pressure loss and fluid properties; Coriolis meters directly measure mass flow through oscillating tubes. Density, gas entrainment and calibration affect their accuracy.

Overcurrent protection must distinguish.en: Overcurrent protection must distinguish overload, short circuit and inrush, with protection selectivity coordinated across upstream/downstream breakers. Trip curves and interrupting ratings are equipment-specific.

Parallel indexing (PI) provides a radar-.en: Parallel indexing (PI) provides a radar-based monitoring line offset from the planned track to help maintain a safe passing distance from fixed charted features. It is not an independent position fix or a substitute for lookout.

Parametric rolling arises from periodic.en: Parametric rolling arises from periodic stability variation as waves encounter the hull. It can grow in head or following seas, depending on ship geometry, wave encounter period, natural rolling and speed, and threatens deck cargo securing.

Passage monitoring continuously verifies.en: Passage monitoring continuously verifies progress against the approved plan through independent fixes, guard zones, wheel-over confirmation and updates for actual traffic and environment.

Passage planning is a berth-to-berth pro.en: Passage planning is a berth-to-berth process of appraisal, planning, execution and monitoring. A route drawn through an ENC is only one part: safety depth/contour, squat, tidal margins, prohibited areas, MSI and contingency actions need evaluation.

Pilot transfer safety depends on approve.en: Pilot transfer safety depends on approved pilot ladder construction, correct rigging and securing, suitable deck lighting and trained supervision. A ladder's age or appearance alone does not establish safe condition.

Pilotage does not relieve the Master or.en: Pilotage does not relieve the Master or officer in charge of the navigational watch of their safety duties. The master–pilot exchange must cover vessel handling limits, communication, route, tugs and any agreed abort decisions.

PLC input/output modules translate field.en: PLC input/output modules translate field signals to controller logic and outputs. A valid CPU state does not prove every I/O signal is physically healthy, especially with open-circuit, stuck or inverted contacts.

Pollution prevention and fuel system dec.en: Pollution prevention and fuel system decision

Port State Control may examine whether c.en: Port State Control may examine whether charts/publications are adequate and updated, critical alarms are functional and crew are familiar with approved procedures. Demonstrated operation and actual records are stronger evidence than generic compliance claims.

Portable extinguishers must be matched t.en: Portable extinguishers must be matched to the fuel, fire class and electrical risk, and their availability does not replace alarm raising or escape-route assessment. Fire class terminology may vary by jurisdiction.

Position coordinates must identify latit.en: Position coordinates must identify latitude and longitude hemispheres together with the chart datum; a coordinate without N/S or E/W can produce a gross position error.

Position DOP (PDOP) reflects the three-d.en: Position DOP (PDOP) reflects the three-dimensional geometry of satellites in the positioning solution, while HDOP and VDOP reflect horizontal and vertical geometric effects. These are dimensionless multipliers, not position errors expressed in metres.

Post-collision response prioritises pers.en: Post-collision response prioritises personnel safety, watertight integrity, pollution control and accurate contact with authorities and neighbouring vessels. Liability arguments should not displace emergency checks.

PPE is the last layer after elimination,.en: PPE is the last layer after elimination, isolation and engineered safeguards. A Job Safety Analysis must consider dynamic energy sources, work interfaces, simultaneous operations and a stop-work trigger.

Practical machinery and shipboard risk a.en: Practical machinery and shipboard risk analysis

Prevention of harassment and violence re.en: Prevention of harassment and violence requires safe reporting, protection from retaliation and a fair, authorised investigation. Immediate safeguarding is distinct from the later determination of facts.

Preventive maintenance is scheduled from.en: Preventive maintenance is scheduled from maker guidance, equipment running hours, duty and criticality; a fixed calendar interval alone may be insufficient. Records must distinguish inspection, actual overhaul and deferred work.

Progressive flooding develops when initi.en: Progressive flooding develops when initial water ingress spreads through additional boundaries such as ducts, penetrations, doors and vents. Initial dry soundings do not rule out later loss of residual stability.

Proportional action reacts to present co.en: Proportional action reacts to present control error, integral action accumulates error over time, and derivative action reacts to its rate of change. Aggressive integral settings may cause windup when an actuator saturates.

Radar range measurements can establish a.en: Radar range measurements can establish an independent position fix when suitable land features and geometric intersection are available. Radar bearings may be less accurate than ranges depending on beamwidth and gyro-heading errors; chart and radar must use a consistent datum.

Refrigeration coefficient of performance.en: Refrigeration coefficient of performance relates heat removed at the evaporator to the work input over an agreed measurement boundary. It can exceed one because the system transports heat rather than converting work directly into cooling.

Reliability-centred maintenance chooses.en: Reliability-centred maintenance chooses run-to-failure, scheduled replacement, condition monitoring or functional testing based on credible failure modes and consequences. The cheapest immediate maintenance task may not minimise safety risk.

Remote quick-closing valves are intended.en: Remote quick-closing valves are intended to isolate fuel supply rapidly during a fire, typically without requiring entry to the affected space. Testing and resetting may have serious operational consequences.

Reserve GMDSS power must sustain require.en: Reserve GMDSS power must sustain required radio functions through approved supply arrangements and maintained batteries. Battery open-circuit voltage does not establish usable capacity under load.

Residual fuel catalytic fines are hard a.en: Residual fuel catalytic fines are hard aluminosilicate particles from refining, often assessed using aluminium plus silicon concentration. Separator efficiency, correct settling and cold/viscous fuel conditions determine abrasive particle exposure at engine injection.

Reverse osmosis drives seawater through.en: Reverse osmosis drives seawater through semipermeable membranes at pressure above osmotic pressure. Product-water quality, filter differential pressure and membrane limits must all be managed.

Rule 8 avoidance action should be positi.en: Rule 8 avoidance action should be positive, made in ample time and with due regard to good seamanship. A succession of small adjustments may obscure intent and fail to achieve adequate separation.

SAR communications separate alert receip.en: SAR communications separate alert receipt, on-scene coordination, search planning and rescue execution. The duty to assist and the authority of designated coordinators depend on the actual situation and governing plans.

Search and rescue communication distingu.en: Search and rescue communication distinguishes the MRCC, an appointed On-Scene Coordinator and individual assisting units. A first-arriving merchant ship must not assume unrestricted command authority.

Set indicates the direction the current.en: Set indicates the direction the current flows toward and drift its speed; vector additions should use ground-referenced units and identical time intervals. The heading/course-through-water vector must be kept distinct from COG.

Ship Security Assessment, approved Ship.en: Ship Security Assessment, approved Ship Security Plan and security levels determine authorised access and incident response. SSAS security alerts must not be confused with DSC or EPIRB distress broadcasts.

Significant wave height is a statistical.en: Significant wave height is a statistical measure, commonly the average of the highest third of waves, not a ceiling on individual waves. Wave period and direction strongly influence ship motions.

Since the 2024 GMDSS modernization, A3 i.en: Since the 2024 GMDSS modernization, A3 is defined relative to the coverage of a recognized mobile satellite service supported by the ship earth station fitted on board, outside A1 and A2. A4 is everything outside that ship's applicable A1/A2/A3 coverage.

SOLAS prescribes safety requirements and.en: SOLAS prescribes safety requirements and ISM implements a company and shipboard Safety Management System. Equipment presence, valid certificates and personnel competence each require separate evidence.

Standard Marine Communication Phrases mi.en: Standard Marine Communication Phrases minimise misunderstandings between VTS, pilots, bridge teams and ships. Course, speed, distance and urgency must be spoken and read back without ambiguity.

Standing orders and Master's night order.en: Standing orders and Master's night orders define bridge watch escalation triggers. Calling the Master is an additional safety measure and never transfers the watch officer's immediate duty to avoid danger.

Steering redundancy is meaningful only i.en: Steering redundancy is meaningful only if the backup control path, power availability, local control, communication and changeover procedures work together. The arrangement is installation-specific.

Surface analysis charts locate pressure.en: Surface analysis charts locate pressure centres, fronts, troughs and weather features at a stated valid time. A front's coloured symbols indicate front type and advance direction, while forecast and analysis charts have different time references.

Tank level devices use differing measure.en: Tank level devices use differing measurement principles (radar, differential pressure, float or capacitance). Fluid density, vapour and foaming can affect particular readings; independent high-level alarms must remain functional.

The 2008 IS Code combines mandatory and.en: The 2008 IS Code combines mandatory and recommended criteria, with ship-specific limitations and approved information. Positive initial GM is only one component of the intact stability assessment; the complete righting-arm curve matters.

The first law tracks energy crossing a d.en: The first law tracks energy crossing a defined system boundary as heat and work, plus changes in stored energy. An engine efficiency statement without a clear boundary can omit auxiliaries, exhaust and cooling losses.

The free-surface correction can be repre.en: The free-surface correction can be represented as a virtual rise of G for applicable tanks. Approved stability-booklet tables, density and actual slack-tank states must replace oversimplified constant corrections.

The GZ curve describes righting lever ov.en: The GZ curve describes righting lever over heel angle; the area under the curve represents dynamic stability only under the relevant assumptions. Peak GZ, range and downflooding angle require separate interpretation.

The GZ curve describes righting lever ve.en: The GZ curve describes righting lever versus heel for a specific loading condition. Its peak, positive range, integral and downflooding limits each convey different stability information; identical GM does not imply identical reserve stability.

The integral of GZ over heel angle repre.en: The integral of GZ over heel angle represents the quasi-static dynamic-stability area, expressed in m·rad. Displacement weight times this integral approximates work against heel; it is not a prediction of ship motions in random seas.

The live satellite image could not be lo.en: The live satellite image could not be loaded. Check the connection and press Refresh.

The modernized SOLAS IV GMDSS arrangemen.en: The modernized SOLAS IV GMDSS arrangements recognise applicable mobile satellite services beyond the older Inmarsat-only framing; the ship's certificate and approved equipment determine its actual A3 coverage. GMDSS and e-navigation have related but distinct purposes.

The planning phase converts appraisal ev.en: The planning phase converts appraisal evidence into waypoints and cross-track limits. The plan must account for manoeuvring radius, wheel-over positions, depth constraints, VTS reporting and contingency manoeuvres.

The radio log should distinguish equipme.en: The radio log should distinguish equipment checks, received warnings, tests, actual distress communications and periods when a required watch could not be maintained. Required entries depend on flag, sea area and the vessel's radio arrangements.

The rule of twelfths is a rough semidiur.en: The rule of twelfths is a rough semidiurnal-tide interpolation model, not a replacement for official port-specific tidal predictions, especially with mixed, diurnal or distorted tidal curves.

The Ship Security Alert System is a cove.en: The Ship Security Alert System is a covert security alerting means under ISPS/SOLAS XI-2 arrangements, not the radio distress alert route used by EPIRB or DSC. Recipients and test procedures are governed by the ship security plan.

Time Charter Equivalent is a comparative.en: Time Charter Equivalent is a comparative voyage earnings measure: voyage revenue less voyage-variable expenses, divided by voyage days on the chosen accounting basis. It is not necessarily the owner's net profit.

TMAS provides medical advice at sea; the.en: TMAS provides medical advice at sea; the bridge team must send precise observations and follow qualified medical direction. Initial emergency response should follow the vessel's trained first-aid protocols.

Towline tension reflects dynamic loads,.en: Towline tension reflects dynamic loads, vessel motions and relative movement, not only bollard-pull rating. Towing arrangements also require compatible fittings, release capability and agreed communications.

TPC is the approximate mass necessary to.en: TPC is the approximate mass necessary to change mean draught by 1 cm near the stated waterline, derived from waterplane area and water density. It varies with draught and loading condition.

Tropical cyclone avoidance should use fo.en: Tropical cyclone avoidance should use forecast motion, wind radii, track uncertainty, vessel capability and sea room. Historical 'dangerous semicircle' rules are only one decision aid, not a universal escape plan.

Ultrasonic thickness measurements requir.en: Ultrasonic thickness measurements require the correct material sound velocity, calibration and clean measurement locations. One apparent low reading can be caused by coating, coupling or surface geometry rather than true local corrosion.

Under-keel clearance is a dynamic margin.en: Under-keel clearance is a dynamic margin, not merely charted depth minus draught. Water level, vessel draught, heel, squat and uncertainty in soundings and position contribute to the passage decision.

Valve grinding and lash adjustment resto.en: Valve grinding and lash adjustment restore sealing and correct thermal clearances only within maker tolerances. Overgrinding can damage seat geometry or reduce valve margin, changing heat transfer and reliability.

VFDs vary motor electrical frequency and.en: VFDs vary motor electrical frequency and voltage/current under a drive control scheme, while mechanical limits and thermal cooling remain binding. Harmonics, electromagnetic interference and shaft-bearing effects require system assessment.

VLSFO compliance is not only a sulphur n.en: VLSFO compliance is not only a sulphur number. Different fuel blends may exhibit compatibility and stability problems; viscosity and heating arrangements affect service conditions.

VTS provides local traffic information a.en: VTS provides local traffic information and may issue instructions under local rules, but participation does not remove the Master's safe-navigation responsibilities or COLREG duties.

When vessels are not in sight of one ano.en: When vessels are not in sight of one another in or near restricted visibility, Rule 19 applies instead of the sight-based head-on and crossing allocation. Safe speed and assessment of radar contacts are central.
